about.title: About
story: I'm a Viet-Chinese-American engineer who works on the web. I was born in Ho Chi Minh City and grew up in Eagan, Minnesota, and studied computer science and IT infrastructure at the University of Minnesota.

Before software, I spent a summer on a metal stamping line at my dad's workplace, and another pulling crab cages with my uncle in Morgan City, Louisiana, starting at 3am. Through the cold winters of Minneapolis, I served hot coffee at Caribou, and at night I did some bartending.

I started my career at Target, working on its first design system and on Target.com, then moved to Zoom and to Google, where I was the accessibility lead for Google's support experience. Today I'm a senior engineer at SmartNews in Tokyo.
I'm passionate about fostering a healthy learning culture and creating that space for everyone.
recognition: MN State Champion — One Act Play, Forensics & Speech

work.title: Work
work.intro: Nine years, four companies, one throughline: build for real people, and leave things better than I found them.

points: AI content infrastructure: LLM generation pipelines, editorial consoles, and delivery to web and native apps.
Designed review gates that combine agent and human moderation before AI-generated content publishes.
Led multi-model routing with request tracing and per-model cost attribution.
Ran 60+ product experiments, and drive evaluation and rollout of the engineering toolchain.
Components and layouts for Guided Support Experience and the Help Center.
Founding engineer on the Help Experience design system and its tokens.
Built the Zoom Events app and virtual events platform UI.
Re-architected CI/CD and introduced unit and integration testing.
Founding engineer on a global design system; mentored interns and new grads.
Performance and architecture for Target.com, from React-Redux to Next.js.
Helped launch Target's first design system.
Mentored engineers through the Technology Leadership Program.
